playbook:
- Before the first hide, note who shoots me per the standing order (the boat before me in the cycle) and treat every hide choice as a guess about their firing model, not as randomness for its own sake.
- When hiding, I avoid repeating cells and avoid the cell I just fired at; I track where my shooter has fired across rounds and pick a cell far from their recent shots and from any pattern I have shown.
- When firing under a standing order, I always fire at the ordered target — deviating gains nothing unless the target is Harbor, which I never fire at given the explicit punishment threat, no matter how tempting the payroll looks.
- When choosing a fire cell, I use the target's hide history: if they have repeated a cell or cycled predictably, I fire there; otherwise I spread shots across untried cells instead of repeating the same cell all game. This episode I fired cell 5 at Foxtrot in nearly every round and missed every time — two misses on the same cell means I move on and never return to it.
- If I have no hide history for my target, I vary my shots across the line (low, middle, high) so that at least I gather information about where they are not, rather than shooting blind at one fixed cell.
- When the office tells me my shot result, I always claim it truthfully; the office already knows the true result, so a false claim is pure risk with no gain.
- Before any escort claim or proposal, I check the actual roster of live boats in this episode; I must never name a boat that does not exist.
- Mutual escort (+5 each) is the biggest scoring lever in the game, bigger than any plausible shooting profit, so securing it is my first priority every episode.
- In round 1 I use my note to propose mutual escort to one specific named real boat ("Foxtrot: name me and I'll name you back every round") — a generic broadcast offer to nobody in particular gets ignored.
- Having proposed escort, I must follow through at the escort stage and actually name that boat. This episode I proposed escort in my note and then filed "none" every single round — the proposal alone scores zero, and filing none after proposing wastes the one lever that could have won the game. I name my proposed partner from round 1 onward; if they reciprocate, we both bank +5 per round; if they don't after two rounds, I switch to the other boat and propose to them via note.
- When another boat's note proposes mutual escort, I honor it at the escort stage by naming them that same round — reciprocity must be immediate or the deal dies.
- I do not default to "none" at the escort stage just because no deal is confirmed; naming my most likely partner costs nothing if they don't reciprocate and pays +5 if they do, so an unilateral name beats a certain zero.
- When I am behind late in the game, escort income is still my best recovery tool: +5 per round outpaces hit income, so I keep naming a partner and keep shots on varied cells against the leader.
- In the final round, I still honor any live mutual escort — the +5 counts even with no future — and I only file "none" if no partner ever formed and no note suggests reciprocation.
- Throughout, I keep a simple log of every boat's shots, hides, claims, notes, and escort filings each round; decisions about fire cells and escort partners come from that log, not from gut feel.

1.text:
PLAYBOOK — hx_picket_checker (revised)

Core priorities, in order: (1) mutual escort payouts (+5 each) are the biggest reliable points — I pursue them every round, but only with a partner who actually reciprocates; (2) hiding on edges/corners and rotating works — across six rounds at cells 2, then other edge cells, I was never hit while shooting poorly at everyone else; (3) follow the firing order and report claims truthfully; (4) never fire on Harbor.

Escort stage:
- I never write "none" unless I have clear evidence nobody will reciprocate. Mutual naming pays 5 each, so pairing should happen every round.
- Reciprocation must be verified, not assumed. Across two games, persistent kindly naming of boats that broadcast only "steady on station" has earned me zero escort points — every time. Naming an unresponsive boat earns me nothing; it only costs strategy focus.
- The pivot protocol works mechanically but didn't pay here either: when Echo ignored me I pivoted to Gamma, who also stayed silent. If the whole table is "steady on station" bots, accept it by round 3 and shift fully to defense/offense grinding.
- Round 1–2 I propose a pairing in my note with an explicit, checkable commitment ("Echo: I'll name you; confirm in YOUR note and name me"). One, at most two rounds of silence and I pivot to the other boat with the same explicit offer. Two strikes total and escort income is written off for the game — I treat +5/round as dead and stop mentioning it in notes.
- A partner who confirms in notes but whose salvage doesn't follow gets one correction, then pivot.
- Even in the final round, escort still pays, so I keep naming my most plausible candidate — it costs nothing — but I don't expect income I haven't verified.

Hide stage (validated — keep this):
- Edge and corner cells (1, 2, 8, 9) genuinely work: I hid there repeatedly and took zero hits across the game. Keep defaulting there.
- Rotate among edges so the boat ordered at me can't lock on; don't return to a cell within a couple rounds.
- I avoid the center (4–6) — everyone, including me, seems to aim or hide there.
- If I do get hit, change my whole pattern rather than oscillating near the same area.

Fire stage (weak point — fix this):
- I fired at Gamma six times and hit zero; cell guesses like 7 and 8 produced nothing. Guessing fresh edges was worse here than exploiting history.
- Better: aim at the target's known or most-repeated recent hide behavior if I have any hint of it; if I hit once, stay near that region's habit the next round against the same target.
- With no history, aim at center-adjacent cells (4–6) rather than edges — opponents appear to gravitate center, and my edge guesses all whiffed. (Note the asymmetry: I HIDE on edges because others shoot center; I SHOOT center-ish because others hide there.)
- Vary my own firing cell so my pattern is unreadable if it leaks.

Claim stage:
- Always claim the true private result. It's mandatory and there is no upside in lying.

Note stage:
- Every note does work. "Steady on station" repeated is a hard diagnostic: that boat will never cooperate. Two games now confirm it — treat the sender as a non-partner from round 2.
- One concrete, actionable proposal per note with a demand for a reply in kind, so silence is diagnostic.
- Once both opponents are diagnosed silent, stop spending notes on proposals; use them sparingly or for misdirection about my hiding habits if useful.

Score review: +4 this game (one hit scored, zero hits taken, zero escort income) vs -2 last time. The improvement came entirely from edge-defense keeping me untouched. Escort income has never materialized against silent tables — its ceiling is high but its floor against "steady on station" players is zero. Plan for the floor: probe hard for two rounds, then play the grind game — hide edges, shoot center-ward, claims honest, salvage still attempted cheaply each round.

2.text:
- When the fire stage puts a target to me, I always obey the standing order and fire at my assigned picket target; I never fire on Harbor — the 3-point jettison gain is not worth the standing threat of being put off the board for the rest of the patrol.

- When I claim a shot result, I always report the private result truthfully — hit when it hit, miss when it missed. Claims must match the private result, and a false claim risks a penalty for nothing.

- When I hide, I treat it as pure evasion from the one boat ordered to fire on me. I track which boat that is and which cells I have used, avoid repeating the cell I just hid in, and never reuse any cell on a detectable rhythm. Rotating widely worked this episode — I was fired on six times and never hit — so I prioritize unpredictability over any "safe cell" theory.

- When firing, I vary my cell across rounds and cover cells I have neglected rather than re-firing misses. If I score a hit, I shoot at or immediately adjacent to that cell next round, because hiders anchor once they feel safe — I hit Echo in round 3 and then wandered to distant cells; I should have hammered that cell and its neighbors while Echo was likely frozen there.

- When firing, I avoid firing the cell I am currently hiding in — if my target reasons symmetrically, my own cell is the one they may guess.

- Over six rounds, blind shots hit rarely (I went 1-for-6 and nobody else hit at all). Escort bonuses are worth more than hits (+5 vs +4) and don't depend on luck, so closing an escort deal is my primary scoring plan, not a side quest.

- To close an escort deal: (a) propose in the round-1 note, (b) name exactly one boat by name with the deal stated plainly, (c) repeat the proposal every note until it is confirmed — a single proposal that gets ignored must not be dropped, since my one-off proposals this episode never got traction and "steady on station" partners confirm nothing, (d) treat the deal as confirmed only if their note explicitly names me back.

- Once I have named a boat in a deal, I file the escort claim naming them every round from then on, even without confirmation: naming a boat that doesn't reciprocate costs nothing, and if they ever name me in the same round I collect +5. This episode I repeatedly filed "none" after proposing — that guaranteed zero; filing the claim would have been free upside.

- When reading relayed notes, I scan specifically for any boat naming me in an escort offer; if one does, I accept in my next note and file the escort claim immediately, since reciprocating a confirmed offer is the single biggest scoring play in the game.

- When posting a station note, I never waste it on filler like "steady on station" — I did exactly that for several rounds this episode and it got me nothing. Every note either proposes an escort deal, confirms one, repeats a standing proposal to keep it visible, or shares useful information that buys goodwill.

- When the standings show me behind late in the game, I stay disciplined: keep firing my assigned target, and prioritize the escort claim over squeezing an extra hit, since +5 beats +4.

- When the last round arrives, everything is free: hide somewhere unused, fire my ordered target at my best-guess cell, claim truthfully, and always file the escort claim naming the boat I proposed to (or any boat that has ever named me) — there is no future round for retaliation or wasted effort, and the mutual bonus can only land if I actually file.
